title.zh: 卷七十七 志第五十三 食貨一
title.raw: 卷七十七 志第五十三 食貨一 Volume 77 Treatises 53: Finance and Economics 1

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「取財於地，而取法於天。

translations.literal: The Record says: "Obtain wealth from the earth, and take one's model from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Record states: "Draw wealth from the land, and take Heaven as your model.

sentences.zh: 富國之本，在於農桑。」

translations.literal: The foundation of enriching the state lies in agriculture and sericulture."
translations.idiomatic: The foundation of a wealthy state lies in farming and silk production."

sentences.zh: 明初，沿元之舊，錢法不通而用鈔，又禁民間以銀交易，宜若不便於民。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming, following Yuan practice, coinage did not circulate and paper notes were used instead; private trade in silver was also forbidden — which would seem inconvenient for the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming, following Yuan precedent, coin did not circulate and paper money was used instead; private silver transactions were also banned — measures that would seem to burden the populace.

sentences.zh: 而洪、永、熙、宣之際，百姓充實，府藏衍溢。

translations.literal: Yet during the Hongwu, Yongle, Hongxi, and Xuande reigns, the people were well provided for and the treasury overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under the Hongwu, Yongle, Hongxi, and Xuande emperors, the common people prospered and government storehouses brimmed with surplus.

sentences.zh: 蓋是時，劭農務墾闢，土無萊蕪，人敦本業，又開屯田、中鹽以給邊軍，餫餉不仰藉於縣官，故上下交足，軍民胥裕。

translations.literal: For at that time agriculture was vigorously encouraged and wasteland was reclaimed; no land lay fallow, people devoted themselves to primary occupations; military colonies and the salt-exchange system were also established to supply border troops, so transport grain did not depend on county officials — hence both court and countryside had enough, and army and people alike were affluent.
translations.idiomatic: The reason was that in those years the state pressed hard to encourage farming and open new land; fields were not left wild, and people held faithfully to their base occupations. Military colonies and the salt-exchange system were also set up to feed frontier armies, so supply convoys did not have to rely on county government — and thus both high and low had plenty, soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 其後，屯田壞於豪強之兼併，計臣變鹽法。

translations.literal: Later, military colonies were ruined by powerful families' encroachments, and finance officials altered the salt laws.
translations.idiomatic: Later, military colonies were destroyed through land grabs by powerful magnates, and planning ministers revised the salt regulations.

sentences.zh: 於是邊兵悉仰食太倉，轉輸住往不給。

translations.literal: Thereupon border troops all relied on food from the Grand Storehouse, and transport often could not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: Border soldiers then came to depend entirely on the central granary, and supply convoys often failed to meet demand.

sentences.zh: 世宗以後，耗財之道廣，府庫匱竭。

translations.literal: After the Jiajing Emperor, channels of expenditure multiplied and the treasury was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiajing reign, avenues of spending multiplied and the public coffers ran dry.

sentences.zh: 神宗乃加賦重徵，礦稅四出，移正供以實左藏。

translations.literal: The Shenzong Emperor then added levies and imposed heavy taxes; mining levies were levied everywhere, and regular tribute was diverted to fill the left treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanli Emperor responded with heavier assessments and surcharges; mining taxes sprang up on all sides, and regular revenue streams were diverted to fill the left-hand vault.

sentences.zh: 中涓羣小，橫斂侵漁。

translations.literal: Eunuchs and petty minions exacted at will and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs and their petty hangers-on levied at will and preyed on the people.

sentences.zh: 民多逐末，田卒汙萊。

translations.literal: Many people pursued secondary trades, and fields in the end became wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: The people turned increasingly to commerce, and farmland in the end lay fallow and overgrown.

sentences.zh: 吏不能拊循，而覆侵刻之。

translations.literal: Officials could not comfort and guide them, but instead compounded extortion.
translations.idiomatic: Officials failed to soothe and guide them, and instead added fresh exactions.

sentences.zh: 海內困敝，而儲積益以空乏。

translations.literal: The empire grew impoverished, while reserves became ever more depleted.
translations.idiomatic: The realm fell into distress, even as stored grain and coin grew ever emptier.

sentences.zh: 昧者多言復通鈔法可以富國，不知國初之充裕在勤農桑，而不在行鈔法也。

translations.literal: The ignorant often said that restoring paper money could enrich the state, not knowing that early-Ming abundance lay in diligence in farming and sericulture, not in using paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: The misguided often argued that reviving paper currency would enrich the state, unaware that early Ming prosperity came from diligent agriculture and silk production, not from banknote policy.

sentences.zh: 夫韁本節用，為理財之要。

translations.literal: Strengthening the fundamental root and economizing expenditure are the essentials of managing finances.
translations.idiomatic: Strengthening the economic base and practicing frugality are the heart of sound fiscal policy.

sentences.zh: 明一代理財之道，始所以得，終所以失，條其本末，著於篇。

translations.literal: The Ming dynasty's methods of managing wealth throughout the dynasty — how they first gained and finally lost — are set forth in outline, root and branch, in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming approach to state finance — how it first prospered and at last failed — is traced here from beginning to end in this chapter.

sentences.zh: ○戶口田制屯田莊田

translations.literal: ○ Household Registers, Field Systems, Military Colonies, and Manor Lands
translations.idiomatic: ○ Household Registers, Land Tenure, Military Colonies, and Estate Lands

sentences.zh: 太祖籍天下戶口，置戶帖、戶籍，具書名、歲、居地。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor registered the empire's households, establishing household certificates and registers, fully recording name, age, and place of residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor registered households empire-wide, issuing household slips and registers that recorded each person's name, age, and place of residence.

sentences.zh: 籍上戶部，帖給之民。

translations.literal: The registers were submitted to the Ministry of Revenue, and certificates were issued to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Registers were filed with the Ministry of Revenue, and slips were distributed to each household.

sentences.zh: 有司歲計其登耗以聞。

translations.literal: Each year local officials calculated increases and decreases and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Each year local officials tallied gains and losses in population and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 及郊祀，中書省以戶籍陳壇下，薦之天，祭畢而藏之。

translations.literal: At suburban sacrifices, the Secretariat of State presented the household registers before the altar, offered them to Heaven, and after the rite stored them away.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban sacrifices, the Secretariat placed the household registers before the altar, presented them to Heaven, and after the ceremony put them in storage.

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年詔天下編賦役黃冊，以一百十戶為一里，推丁糧多者十戶為長，餘百戶為十甲，甲凡十人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongwu an edict ordered the empire to compile yellow registers for tax and corvée, taking one hundred and ten households as one li; the ten households with the most adult males and grain tax were made leaders, and the remaining hundred households formed ten jia of ten persons each.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 14 (1381) an edict ordered compilation of yellow registers for tax and labor service empire-wide: one hundred and ten households formed a li; the ten households with the heaviest adult-male and grain-tax burden became leaders, and the remaining hundred households were divided into ten jia of ten persons each.

sentences.zh: 歲役裏長一人，甲首一人，董一里一甲之事。

translations.literal: Each year one li chief and one jia head were levied for service, supervising the affairs of one li and one jia.
translations.idiomatic: Each year one li chief and one jia head were called up for duty to oversee the affairs of their li and jia.

sentences.zh: 先後以丁糧多寡為序，凡十年一週，曰排年。

translations.literal: Order was determined by the amount of adult males and grain tax, with a full cycle every ten years, called the rotation of years.
translations.idiomatic: Duty rotated in order of adult-male and grain-tax burden, completing a full cycle every ten years — the pai-nian rotation.

sentences.zh: 在城曰坊，近城曰廂，鄉都曰裏。

translations.literal: Within cities they were called fang; near cities, xiang; in rural districts, li.
translations.idiomatic: Urban units were called fang, suburban ones xiang, and rural districts li.

sentences.zh: 裏編為冊，冊首總為一圖。

translations.literal: Each li was compiled into a register, and the registers for a district were summarized in one chart.
translations.idiomatic: Each li was entered in a register, and the head of each register bore a summary chart for the whole district.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不任役者，附十甲後為畸零。

translations.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless who could not bear corvée were attached after the ten jia as marginal households.
translations.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who could not perform labor service were listed after the ten jia as marginal (jiling) households.

sentences.zh: 僧道給度牒，有田者編冊如民科，無田者亦為畸零。

translations.literal: Monks and Daoists were issued ordination certificates; those with land were entered in registers like commoners for taxation, those without land were also classed as marginal.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and Daoist priests received ordination certificates; those who held land were registered and taxed like commoners, while landless clergy were also counted as marginal households.

sentences.zh: 每十年有司更定其冊，以丁糧增減而升降之。

translations.literal: Every ten years local officials revised the registers, promoting or demoting households according to increases or decreases in adult males and grain tax.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten years local officials revised the registers, adjusting household rank up or down as adult-male and grain-tax obligations rose or fell.

sentences.zh: 冊凡四：一上戶部，其三則布政司、府、縣各存一焉。

translations.literal: There were four copies of each register: one submitted to the Ministry of Revenue, and the other three kept respectively by the provincial administration commission, prefecture, and county.
translations.idiomatic: Each register existed in four copies: one sent to the Ministry of Revenue, and one each retained by the provincial administration commission, the prefecture, and the county.

sentences.zh: 上戶部者，冊面黃紙，故謂之黃冊。

translations.literal: The copy sent to the Ministry of Revenue had yellow paper on its cover, hence it was called the yellow register.
translations.idiomatic: The copy filed with the Ministry of Revenue used yellow paper for its cover — hence the name yellow register (huangce).

sentences.zh: 年終進呈，送後湖東西二庫庋藏之。

translations.literal: At year's end they were presented and sent to the eastern and western storehouses at Rear Lake for storage.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end they were submitted and deposited in the eastern and western archives at Rear Lake.

sentences.zh: 歲命戶科給事中一人、御史二人、戶部主事四人釐校訛舛。

translations.literal: Each year one supervising secretary of the revenue section, two censors, and four principal secretaries of the Ministry of Revenue were ordered to check and correct errors.
translations.idiomatic: Each year one supervising secretary from the revenue section of the Secretariat, two censors, and four Ministry of Revenue principal secretaries were assigned to audit and correct discrepancies.

sentences.zh: 其後黃冊只具文，有司徵稅、編徭，則自為一冊，曰白冊云。

translations.literal: Later the yellow register became a mere formality; when local officials collected taxes and arranged corvée, they compiled their own register, called the white register.
translations.idiomatic: In time the yellow register became a dead letter; for actual tax collection and corvée assignment local officials kept a separate working register known as the white register (baice).

sentences.zh: 凡戶三等：曰民，曰軍，曰匠。

translations.literal: Households were divided into three grades: commoners, military, and artisans.
translations.idiomatic: Households fell into three broad categories: commoners, military, and artisans.

sentences.zh: 民有儒，有醫，有陰陽。

translations.literal: Among commoners were Confucian scholars, physicians, and yin-yang masters.
translations.idiomatic: Commoner households included scholars, physicians, and yin-yang diviners.

sentences.zh: 軍有校尉，有力士，弓、鋪兵。

translations.literal: Among military households were commandants, strongmen, archers, and garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Military households included commandants, strongmen, archers, and garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 匠有廚役、裁縫、馬船之類。

translations.literal: Among artisans were kitchen servants, tailors, horse-boat crews, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Artisan households included kitchen servants, tailors, horse-transport crews, and similar trades.

sentences.zh: 瀕海有鹽竈。

translations.literal: Along the coast were salt-boiler households.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal districts had salt-boiler households.

sentences.zh: 寺有僧，觀有道士。

translations.literal: Monasteries had monks; abbeys had Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist temples held monks; Daoist abbeys held priests.

sentences.zh: 畢以其業著籍。

translations.literal: All were registered according to their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Each was entered in the register according to his trade.

sentences.zh: 人戶以籍為斷，禁數姓合戶附籍。

translations.literal: Personal household status was determined by the register; combining several surnames into one household to attach to another register was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Household status was fixed by registration, and combining several surnames into one household to attach to another register was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 漏口、脫戶，許自實。

translations.literal: Those who had omitted persons or left the register were permitted to report themselves truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Households that had concealed members or dropped off the register were allowed to come forward voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 裏設老人，選年高為眾所服者，導民善，平鄉里爭訟。

translations.literal: Each li appointed elders, choosing those advanced in years whom the multitude respected, to guide the people in virtue and settle village disputes.
translations.idiomatic: Each li appointed elders — respected seniors — to guide the people toward good conduct and mediate local disputes.

sentences.zh: 其人戶避徭役者曰逃戶。

translations.literal: Households that evaded corvée were called fugitive households.
translations.idiomatic: Households that fled to avoid labor service were called fugitive households (taohu).

sentences.zh: 年饑或避兵他徙者曰流民。

translations.literal: Those who moved elsewhere because of famine or to escape warfare were called floating populations.
translations.idiomatic: Those who drifted elsewhere in famine years or to escape warfare were called floating populations (liumin).

sentences.zh: 有故而出僑於外者曰附籍。

translations.literal: Those who for some reason went to sojourn elsewhere were called attached registration.
translations.idiomatic: Those who for some reason went to sojourn elsewhere were called attached-registration households (fuji).

sentences.zh: 朝廷所移民曰移徙。

translations.literal: Populations relocated by the court were called transferred migration.
translations.idiomatic: Populations relocated by government order were called state resettlement (yixi).

sentences.zh: 凡逃戶，明初督令還本籍復業，賜復一年。

translations.literal: As for fugitive households, in early Ming they were urged to return to their original registers and resume their occupations, and were granted one year of tax remission.
translations.idiomatic: In early Ming, fugitive households were pressed to return to their home registers and resume farming, and were granted a one-year tax holiday.

sentences.zh: 老弱不能歸及不願歸者，令在所著籍，授田輸賦。

translations.literal: The aged and weak who could not return, and those unwilling to return, were ordered to register where they were, given land, and required to pay taxes.
translations.idiomatic: The elderly and infirm who could not return, and those who chose not to, were registered where they stood, granted land, and taxed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 正統時，造逃戶周知冊，核其丁糧。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign a comprehensive register of fugitive households was compiled to verify their adult males and grain tax.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhengtong Emperor a comprehensive fugitive-household register was drawn up to verify adult-male and grain-tax obligations.

sentences.zh: 凡流民，英宗令勘籍，編甲互保，屬在所裏長管轄之。

translations.literal: As for floating populations, the Yingzong Emperor ordered investigation of registers, organization into mutual-guarantee jia, and placement under the jurisdiction of local li chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: For floating populations, the Yingzong Emperor ordered registration checks, organization into mutual-guarantee jia groups, and supervision by local li chiefs.

sentences.zh: 設撫民佐貳官。

translations.literal: Assistant officials to pacify the people were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy officials for pacifying the people were appointed.

sentences.zh: 歸本者，勞徠安輯，給牛、種、口糧。

translations.literal: Those returning home were comforted and settled, and given oxen, seed, and rations.
translations.idiomatic: Returnees were welcomed back, settled, and supplied with oxen, seed grain, and food rations.

sentences.zh: 又從河南、山西巡撫于謙言，免流民復業者稅。

translations.literal: Following the proposal of Yu Qian, grand coordinator of Henan and Shanxi, taxes were remitted for floating populations who resumed their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: At the urging of Yu Qian, grand coordinator of Henan and Shanxi, taxes were waived for floating populations who returned to farming.

sentences.zh: 成化初，荊、襄寇亂，流民百萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign, bandit turmoil in Jing and Xiang produced a million floating people.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign, rebellion in the Jing and Xiang region drove a million people into flight.

sentences.zh: 項忠、楊璿為湖廣巡撫，下令逐之，弗率者戍邊，死者無算。

translations.literal: Xiang Zhong and Yang Xuan, as grand coordinators of Huguang, ordered them expelled; those who did not comply were sent to garrison the border, and the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: As grand coordinators of Huguang, Xiang Zhong and Yang Xuan ordered the refugees expelled; those who refused were banished to frontier garrison duty, and untold numbers died.

sentences.zh: 祭酒周洪謨著《流民說》，引東晉時僑置郡縣之法，使近者附籍，遠者設州縣以撫之。

translations.literal: Chancellor of the Directorate Zhou Hongmo wrote "On Floating Populations," citing the Eastern Jin method of establishing attached prefectures and counties: those nearby were to attach to local registers, those far away were to have prefectures and counties set up to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hongmo, chancellor of the Directorate of Education, wrote On Floating Populations, citing the Eastern Jin practice of establishing attached prefectures and counties: nearby refugees would register locally; distant ones would receive new administrative units for resettlement.

sentences.zh: 都御史李賓上其說。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Li Bin presented this proposal to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Li Bin submitted the proposal to the throne.

sentences.zh: 憲宗命原傑出撫，招流民十二萬戶，給閒田，置鄖陽府，立上津等縣統治之。

translations.literal: The Xianzong Emperor ordered Yuan Jie to go out as pacification commissioner; he recruited one hundred and twenty thousand floating households, granted idle land, established Yunyang Prefecture, and set up Shangjin and other counties to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenghua Emperor dispatched Yuan Jie as pacification commissioner; he resettled one hundred twenty thousand floating households on vacant land, created Yunyang Prefecture, and established Shangjin and other counties to administer them.

sentences.zh: 河南巡撫張瑄亦請輯西北流民。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuan, grand coordinator of Henan, also requested to settle floating populations of the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan, grand coordinator of Henan, likewise petitioned to resettle northwestern refugees.

sentences.zh: 帝從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted the request.

sentences.zh: 凡附籍者，正統時，老疾致仕事故官家屬，離本籍千里者許收附，不及千里者發還。

translations.literal: As for attached registration, in the Zhengtong reign the families of officials who retired due to age, illness, or bereavement were permitted to attach if more than a thousand li from their original register; if less than a thousand li they were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: For attached registration, under Zhengtong rules the families of officials who retired for age, illness, or bereavement could register locally if more than a thousand li from home; within a thousand li they were sent back.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，令民籍者收附，軍、匠、竈役冒民籍者發還。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai reign commoner registrants were permitted to attach, while military, artisan, and salt-boiler households falsely posing as commoners were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingtai Emperor, genuine commoners could attach locally, but military, artisan, and salt-boiler households falsely registered as commoners were returned to their original status.

sentences.zh: 其移徙者，明初，當徙蘇、鬆、嘉、湖、杭民之無田者四千餘戶，往耕臨濠，給牛、種、車、糧，以資遣之，三年不徵其稅。

translations.literal: As for state resettlement, in early Ming more than four thousand landless households from Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Hangzhou were moved to farm at Linhao; they were given oxen, seed, carts, and grain for their journey, and were exempt from taxes for three years.
translations.idiomatic: For state resettlement, early Ming authorities moved more than four thousand landless households from Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Hangzhou to farm at Linhao, supplying oxen, seed, carts, and travel grain, with a three-year tax exemption.

sentences.zh: 徐達平沙漠，徙北平山後民三萬五千八百餘戶，散處諸府衛，籍為軍者給衣糧，民給田。

translations.literal: When Xu Da pacified the desert, he moved more than thirty-five thousand eight hundred households from north of the Yan mountains to Beiping, dispersing them among various prefectures and guards; those registered as military were given clothing and grain, commoners were given land.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Da pacified the northern steppe, he resettled more than thirty-five thousand eight hundred households from beyond the Yan mountains across Beiping prefectures and guards; military registrants received clothing and rations, civilians received farmland.

sentences.zh: 又以沙漠遺民三萬二千八百餘戶屯田北平，置屯二百五十四，開地千三百四十三頃。

translations.literal: He also settled more than thirty-two thousand eight hundred desert remnant households in military colonies in Beiping, establishing two hundred fifty-four colonies and opening one thousand three hundred forty-three qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: He also settled more than thirty-two thousand eight hundred steppe remnant households in Beiping military colonies — two hundred fifty-four colonies opening one thousand three hundred forty-three qing of land.

sentences.zh: 復徙江南民十四萬於鳳陽。

translations.literal: He further moved one hundred forty thousand Jiangnan people to Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He further resettled one hundred forty thousand people from the lower Yangtze region at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 戶部郎中劉九皋言：「古狹鄉之民，聽遷之寬鄉，欲地無遺利，人無失業也。」

translations.literal: Liu Jiugao, director in the Ministry of Revenue, said: "In antiquity people from crowded districts were permitted to move to spacious ones, so that no land would lie unused and no person be without occupation."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jiugao, a director in the Ministry of Revenue, said: "In antiquity people from overcrowded districts were allowed to move to underpopulated ones, so that no land went unused and no one lacked a livelihood."

sentences.zh: 太祖採其議，遷山西澤、潞民於河北。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor adopted his proposal and moved the people of Ze and Lu to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor adopted the proposal and resettled people from Shanxi's Ze and Lu prefectures in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 眾屢徙浙西及山西民於滁、和、北平、山東、河南。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he moved people from western Zhejiang and Shanxi to Chu, He, Beiping, Shandong, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly resettled people from western Zhejiang and Shanxi to Chu, He, Beiping, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 又徙登、萊、青民於東昌、兗州。

translations.literal: He also moved people from Deng, Lai, and Qing to Dongchang and Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also moved people from Deng, Lai, and Qing prefectures to Dongchang and Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又徙直隸、浙江民二萬戶於京師，充倉腳夫。

translations.literal: He also moved twenty thousand households from Zhili and Zhejiang to the capital to serve as granary porters.
translations.idiomatic: He also moved twenty thousand households from Zhili and Zhejiang to the capital as granary porters.

sentences.zh: 太祖時徙民最多，其間有以罪徙者。

translations.literal: Resettlement was greatest under the Taizu Emperor; among those moved, some were banished for crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Resettlement peaked under the Hongwu Emperor; some deportees were criminals exiled as punishment.

sentences.zh: 建文帝命武康伯徐理往北平度地處之。

translations.literal: The Jianwen Emperor ordered Marquis of Wukang Xu Li to go to Beiping to survey land and settle people.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianwen Emperor sent Marquis of Wukang Xu Li to Beiping to survey land and arrange resettlement.

sentences.zh: 成祖核太原、平陽、澤、潞、遼、沁、汾丁多田少及無田之家，分其丁口以實北平。

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor audited households in Taiyuan, Pingyang, Ze, Lu, Liao, Qin, and Fen with many adult males but little land or no land at all, and distributed their persons to populate Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor audited households in Taiyuan, Pingyang, Ze, Lu, Liao, Qin, and Fen with many adult males but little or no land, and redistributed their members to populate Beiping.

sentences.zh: 自是以後，移徙者鮮矣。

translations.literal: After this, state resettlement became rare.
translations.idiomatic: After that, large-scale state resettlement became rare.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖設養濟院收無告者，月給糧。

translations.literal: At first the Taizu Emperor established relief hospices to take in those with no one to care for them, granting grain each month.
translations.idiomatic: Early on the Hongwu Emperor established relief hospices for those with no one to support them, issuing monthly grain rations.

sentences.zh: 設漏澤園葬貧民。

translations.literal: He established public burial grounds to inter the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He established public burial grounds (louzeyuan) for the poor.

sentences.zh: 天下府州縣立義塚。

translations.literal: Charitable burial grounds were established in prefectures, departments, and counties throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Charitable burial grounds were established in prefectures and counties empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 又行養老之政，民年八十以上賜爵。

translations.literal: He also implemented policies to support the aged, granting noble ranks to commoners eighty years of age or older.
translations.idiomatic: He also enacted policies honoring the elderly, granting noble ranks to commoners aged eighty or above.

sentences.zh: 復下詔優恤遭難兵民。

translations.literal: He further issued edicts granting favorable relief to soldiers and civilians who had suffered hardship.
translations.idiomatic: He further issued edicts granting special relief to soldiers and civilians who had suffered wartime hardship.

sentences.zh: 然懲元末豪強侮貧弱，立法多右貧抑富。

translations.literal: Yet to punish the powerful families of late Yuan who had bullied the poor and weak, legislation often favored the poor and restrained the rich.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to punish late-Yuan magnates who had bullied the poor, legislation often favored the poor and restrained the wealthy.

sentences.zh: 嘗命戶部籍浙江等九布政司、應天十八府州富民萬四千三百餘戶，以次召見，徙其家以實京師，謂之富戶。

translations.literal: He once ordered the Ministry of Revenue to register more than fourteen thousand three hundred wealthy households from nine provincial administration commissions including Zhejiang and eighteen prefectures and departments of Yingtian; they were summoned in turn and their families moved to populate the capital — called wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: He once ordered the Ministry of Revenue to register more than fourteen thousand three hundred wealthy households from nine provinces including Zhejiang and from eighteen Yingtian prefectures; summoned in turn, their families were moved to the capital — the so-called wealthy households (fuhu).

sentences.zh: 成祖時，復選應天、浙江富民三千戶，充北京宛、大二縣廂長，附籍京師，仍應本籍徭役。

translations.literal: Under the Chengzu Emperor, three thousand wealthy households from Yingtian and Zhejiang were again selected to serve as ward chiefs of Wan and Da counties in Beijing, attaching their registers to the capital while still bearing corvée in their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongle Emperor, three thousand wealthy households from Yingtian and Zhejiang were again selected as ward chiefs for Wan and Da counties in Beijing, registering in the capital while still liable for corvée at home.

sentences.zh: 供給日久，貧乏逃竄，輒選其本籍殷實戶僉補。

translations.literal: As supplies continued over time, impoverishment and flight occurred, and wealthy households from their home districts were conscripted to fill the vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Over time many were ruined and fled; wealthy households from their home districts were then conscripted to replace them.

sentences.zh: 宣德間定制，逃者發邊充軍，官司鄰裏隱匿者俱坐罪。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign regulations were fixed: fugitives were sent to the border as soldiers, and officials and neighbors who concealed them were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande rules, fugitives were banished to frontier military service, and officials or neighbors who concealed them were punished.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年始免解在逃富戶，每戶徵銀三兩，與廂民助役。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi the practice of escorting fugitive wealthy households back began to be waived; each household paid three taels of silver to assist ward residents in corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 5 (1492) the state stopped forcibly returning fugitive wealthy households; each household instead paid three taels of silver to help ward residents meet labor obligations.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中減為二兩，以充邊餉。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign it was reduced to two taels, applied to border supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jiajing Emperor the levy was reduced to two taels, earmarked for frontier supplies.

sentences.zh: 太祖立法之意，本仿漢徙富民實關中之制，其後事久弊生，遂為厲階。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor's intent in legislating was originally to imitate the Han practice of moving wealthy households to populate Guanzhong; later, as time passed abuses arose, and it became a source of harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor's policy imitated the Han practice of resettling wealthy households to populate Guanzhong; in time abuses accumulated until it became a source of widespread harm.

sentences.zh: 戶口之數，增減不一，其可考者，洪武二十六年，天下戶一千六十五萬二千八百七十，口六千五十四萬五千八百十二。

translations.literal: Household and population figures rose and fell unevenly; where records survive, in the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu the empire had ten million six hundred fifty-two thousand eight hundred seventy households and sixty million five hundred forty-five thousand eight hundred twelve persons.
translations.idiomatic: Population figures fluctuated unevenly; where records survive, in Hongwu 26 (1393) the empire registered 10,652,870 households and 60,545,812 persons.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，戶九百十一萬三千四百四十六，口五千三百二十八萬一千一百五十八。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi there were nine million one hundred thirteen thousand four hundred forty-six households and fifty-three million two hundred eighty-one thousand one hundred fifty-eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 4 (1491) there were 9,113,446 households and 53,281,158 persons.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年，戶一千六十二萬一千四百三十六，口六千六十九萬二千八百五十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli there were ten million six hundred twenty-one thousand four hundred thirty-six households and sixty million six hundred ninety-two thousand eight hundred fifty-six persons.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 6 (1578) there were 10,621,436 households and 60,692,856 persons.

sentences.zh: 太祖當兵燹之後，戶口顧極盛。

translations.literal: Under the Taizu Emperor, coming after the ravages of war, the population was nevertheless extremely large.
translations.idiomatic: Remarkably, under the Hongwu Emperor — right after the devastation of war — registered population was at its peak.

sentences.zh: 其後承平日久，反不及焉。

translations.literal: Later, after long years of peace, it fell short of that level instead.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after long years of peace, the count actually fell short of that peak.

sentences.zh: 靖難兵起，淮以北鞠為茂草，其時民數反增於前。

translations.literal: When the Jingnan campaign erupted, north of the Huai turned to wild grass, yet at that time the population count actually increased over the previous figure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingnan civil war broke out, the land north of the Huai was laid waste, yet registered population actually rose above the previous count.

sentences.zh: 後乃遞減，至天順間為最衰。

translations.literal: Afterward it declined in succession, reaching its lowest point in the Tianshun reign.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter it declined steadily, hitting its lowest point under the Tianshun Emperor.

sentences.zh: 成、弘繼盛，正德以後又減。

translations.literal: The Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns saw renewed prosperity, but after Zhengde it declined again.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns saw recovery, but after the Zhengde Emperor numbers fell again.

sentences.zh: 戶口所以減者，周忱謂：「投倚於豪門，或冒匠竄兩京，或冒引賈四方，舉家舟居，莫可蹤跡也。」

translations.literal: The reason population declined, Zhou Chen said, was: "They threw themselves on powerful families' protection, or falsely registered as artisans and hid in the two capitals, or falsely registered as merchants and traveled the four quarters; whole families lived on boats with no trace to be found."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chen explained the decline: "People attached themselves to powerful households, falsely registered as artisans and hid in the two capitals, or falsely registered as merchants and roamed the empire — whole families living on boats, beyond any official trace."

sentences.zh: 而要之，戶口增減，由於政令張弛。

translations.literal: In sum, increases and decreases in population depended on whether government orders were strict or lax.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, population rises and falls reflected whether government enforcement was strict or lax.

sentences.zh: 故宣宗嘗與羣臣論歷代戶口，以為「其盛也，本於休養生息，其衰也，由土木兵戎」，殆篤論云。

translations.literal: Therefore the Xuande Emperor once discussed with his ministers the household registers of successive dynasties, holding that "when flourishing, it rested on nourishing life and letting the people rest; when declining, it was due to civil construction projects and warfare" — this was indeed a sound judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande Emperor once discussed historical population trends with his ministers, holding that "when flourishing, it rested on nourishing life and letting the people rest; when declining, it was due to civil construction and warfare" — a judgment that rings true.

sentences.zh: 明土田之制，凡二等：曰官田，曰民田。

translations.literal: The Ming system for land had two grades in all: called official land and commoner land.
translations.idiomatic: Ming land tenure divided the realm into two categories: official land and private (commoner) land.

sentences.zh: 初，官田皆宋、元時入官田地。

translations.literal: At first, official land was all land that had entered official ownership in Song and Yuan times.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, official land consisted of fields that had been confiscated or registered as state property under the Song and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 厥後有還官田，沒官田，斷入官田，學田，皇莊，牧馬草場，城鵒需苜蓿地，牲地，園陵墳地，公佔隙地，諸王、公主、勳戚、大臣、內監、寺觀賜乞莊田，百官職田，邊臣養廉田，軍、民、商屯田，通謂之官田。

translations.literal: Afterward there were restored-to-the-state lands, confiscated lands, lands adjudicated into state ownership, school fields, imperial estates, horse-pasture grounds, lands for city walls and suburbs requiring alfalfa, sacrificial lands, garden-tomb and mausoleum lands, publicly occupied vacant lands, estate fields granted or petitioned for by princes, princesses, meritorious kinsmen, great ministers, eunuchs, and Buddhist or Daoist temples, official salary fields for all ranks, border officials' integrity-support fields, and military, civilian, and merchant colony fields — all collectively termed official land.
translations.idiomatic: Later categories of official land included restored state fields, confiscated property, adjudicated seizures, school lands, imperial estates, cavalry pastures, alfalfa grounds for city walls and suburbs, lands for ritual sacrifice, mausoleum and tomb precincts, publicly held vacant plots, estates granted to princes, princesses, noble kinsmen, senior officials, eunuchs, and temples, fields assigned to support official salaries, "integrity cultivation" grants for border officials, and military, civilian, and merchant colony fields — all classified together as official land.

sentences.zh: 其餘為民田。

translations.literal: The remainder were commoner land.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else counted as private commoner land.

sentences.zh: 元季喪亂，版籍多亡，田賦無準。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan there was chaotic devastation; household registers were mostly lost, and land tax had no standard.
translations.idiomatic: The chaos at the end of the Yuan destroyed most registers, leaving land taxation without a reliable basis.

sentences.zh: 明太祖即帝位，遣周鑄等百六十四人，核浙西田畝，定其賦稅。

translations.literal: When Ming Taizu took the throne, he sent Zhou Zhu and others, one hundred sixty-four persons in all, to verify fields and mu in western Zhejiang and fix their land tax.
translations.idiomatic: On ascending the throne, Hongwu dispatched Zhou Zhu and 163 others to survey western Zhejiang's fields and establish tax rates.

sentences.zh: 復命戶部核實天下土田。

translations.literal: He again ordered the Ministry of Revenue to verify land throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Ministry of Revenue to verify landholdings empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 而兩浙富民畏避徭役，大率以田產寄他戶，謂之鐵腳詭寄。

translations.literal: Yet wealthy households in the two Zhes feared and evaded corvée; for the most part they lodged their estates under other households' names — called iron-foot fraudulent registration.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families in the two Zhe regions, seeking to evade corvée, commonly registered their property under other households' names — the practice known as iron-foot fraudulent registration.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十年命國子生武淳等分行州縣，隨糧定區。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Hongwu he ordered imperial academy students such as Wu Chun to go out to prefectures and counties, fixing districts according to grain quotas.
translations.idiomatic: In 1387 Hongwu sent imperial academy students including Wu Chun to counties and prefectures to delineate tax districts according to grain quotas.

sentences.zh: 區設糧長四人，量度田畝方圓，次以字型大小，悉書主名及田之丈尺，編類為冊，狀如魚鱗，號曰魚鱗圖冊。

translations.literal: Each district had four grain chiefs; they measured the square and circular extent of fields, arranged them by the size of character forms, wrote out in full owners' names and the foot-measures of fields, compiled them into books shaped like fish scales, and called them fish-scale registers.
translations.idiomatic: Each district appointed four grain chiefs who measured plots, arranged records by script size, listed every owner with field dimensions, and compiled booklets shaped like fish scales — the fish-scale register.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔天下編黃冊，以戶為主，詳具舊管、新收、開除、實在之數為四柱式。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had ordered the empire to compile yellow registers, taking households as primary, detailing fully the four-column format of formerly administered, newly received, struck off, and actually existing figures.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier edicts had required yellow registers organized by household, using the four-column format (former holdings, additions, removals, and current totals).

sentences.zh: 而魚鱗圖冊以土田為主，諸原阪、墳衍、下隰、沃瘠、沙鹵之別畢具。

translations.literal: The fish-scale register took land as primary; distinctions among uplands, slopes, marshy flats, low wetlands, fertile and lean, sandy and saline soils were all fully set out.
translations.idiomatic: Fish-scale registers focused on land itself, recording every category from uplands and slopes to wetlands, and noting fertile, poor, sandy, and saline soils.

sentences.zh: 魚鱗冊為經，土田之訟質焉。

translations.literal: The fish-scale book served as warp; land lawsuits were decided by it.
translations.idiomatic: The fish-scale register served as the warp thread — the authoritative record for land disputes.

sentences.zh: 黃冊為緯，賦役之法定焉。

translations.literal: The yellow register served as weft; the law of taxes and corvée was fixed by it.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow register served as the weft, fixing the basis for tax and corvée obligations.

sentences.zh: 凡質賣田土，備書稅糧科則，官為籍記之，毋令產去稅存以為民害。

translations.literal: Whenever fields were bought or sold on pledge, tax grain and tax categories were fully written; officials recorded them in registers, so that property would not depart while tax remained to harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: Sales of land had to document tax obligations; officials recorded transfers to prevent the bane of sold property still carrying the seller's tax burden.

sentences.zh: 又以中原田多蕪，命省臣議，計民授田。

translations.literal: Also because fields in the central plain were largely fallow, he ordered provincial ministers to deliberate on allotting fields to the people by calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Because much central China land lay fallow, he ordered provincial officials to devise plans for allocating fields to the people.

sentences.zh: 設司農司，開治河南，掌其事。

translations.literal: He established the Director-General of Agriculture Office, opening and governing Henan, to take charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He set up the Directorate of Agriculture in Henan to oversee the program.

sentences.zh: 臨濠之田，驗其丁力，計畝給之，毋許兼併。

translations.literal: At Linhao, fields were allotted by verifying adult male labor and calculating mu granted; merger was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Linhao land was distributed according to household labor capacity, with mergers forbidden.

sentences.zh: 北方近城地多不治，召民耕，人給十五畝，蔬地二畝，免租三年。

translations.literal: In the north, land near cities was largely uncultivated; commoners were summoned to farm — each person was given fifteen mu, two mu for vegetables, with rent remitted for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Uncultivated land near northern cities was opened to settlers, who received fifteen mu of grain land plus two mu for vegetables, tax-free for three years.

sentences.zh: 每歲中書省奏天下墾田數，少者畝以千計，多者至二十餘萬。

translations.literal: Each year the Secretariat reported empire-wide reclaimed-field figures: the fewest counted in thousands of mu, the most reaching more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the central government reported reclaimed acreage — from thousands of mu in some regions to over 200,000 in others.

sentences.zh: 官給牛及農具者，乃收其稅，額外墾荒者永不起科。

translations.literal: Those to whom the state gave oxen and farm implements were then taxed; those reclaiming wasteland beyond quota were forever exempt from tax assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Settlers who received government oxen and tools paid taxes; those who reclaimed wasteland beyond allotments enjoyed permanent tax exemption.

sentences.zh: 二十六年核天下土田，總八百五十萬七千六百二十三頃，蓋駸駸無棄土矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year land throughout the empire was verified, totaling eight million five hundred seven thousand six hundred twenty-three qing — truly there was no abandoned soil.
translations.idiomatic: The 1393 census recorded 8,507,623 qing of land empire-wide — nearly every foot of soil was under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 凡田以近郭為上地，迤遠為中地、下地。

translations.literal: As a rule, fields near the outer city were upper land; progressively distant were middle and lower land.
translations.idiomatic: Fields were graded by distance from the city wall: nearest as upper-grade, farther as middle or lower.

sentences.zh: 五尺為步，步二百四十為畝，畝百為頃。

translations.literal: Five feet made one bu; two hundred forty bu made one mu; one hundred mu made one qing.
translations.idiomatic: A bu was five feet, 240 bu made a mu, and 100 mu made a qing.

sentences.zh: 太祖仍元裏社制，河北諸州縣土著者以社分裏甲，遷民分屯之地以屯分裏甲。

translations.literal: Taizu followed the Yuan li-she system: in various prefectures and counties of Hebei, native settlers divided li-jia by she; resettled colonists in colony areas divided li-jia by colony.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu retained the Yuan li-she structure: in Hebei, natives were organized into li-jia by community (she), while resettled colonists were organized by colony.

sentences.zh: 社民先佔畝廣，屯民新佔畝狹，故屯地謂之小畝，社地謂之廣畝。

translations.literal: She inhabitants had occupied mu broadly at first; colonists newly occupied narrow mu, so colony land was called small mu and she land was called broad mu.
translations.idiomatic: Established communities held wider plots while newer colonists received narrower ones — "small mu" for colony fields versus "broad mu" for community fields.

sentences.zh: 至宣德間，墾荒田永不起科及洿下斥鹵無糧者，皆核入賦額，數溢於舊。

translations.literal: By the Xuande reign, wasteland forever exempt from tax and low saline land paying no grain were all verified into the tax quota; figures exceeded the old.
translations.idiomatic: By Xuande's time, formerly tax-exempt reclaimed and saline wasteland was folded into assessments, swelling totals beyond earlier records.

sentences.zh: 有司乃以大畝當小畝以符舊額，有數畝當一畝者。

translations.literal: Local officials then used large mu in place of small mu to match old quotas; in places several mu counted as one mu.
translations.idiomatic: Officials substituted larger measure for smaller to meet old quotas — in some cases several mu counted as one.

sentences.zh: 步尺參差不一，人得以意贏縮，土地不均，未有如北方者。

translations.literal: Bu and foot-measures were irregular; people could expand or shrink at will; land was unequal — nowhere as in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Inconsistent measuring rods let officials manipulate acreage; nowhere was land inequality worse than in the north.

sentences.zh: 貴州田無頃畝尺籍，悉徵之土官。

translations.literal: Guizhou had no qing, mu, or foot registers for fields; all were levied on native officials.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou kept no standard land registers; taxes were levied entirely through native chieftains.

sentences.zh: 而諸處土田，日久頗淆亂，與黃冊不符。

translations.literal: Yet land registers everywhere over time grew quite confused and did not accord with yellow registers.
translations.idiomatic: Over time local land records diverged widely from the yellow registers.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年，天下土田止四百二十二萬八千五十八頃，官田視民田得七之一。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi, empire-wide land totaled only four million two hundred twenty-eight thousand fifty-eight qing; official land compared with commoner land was one in seven.
translations.idiomatic: By 1502 registered land had fallen to 4,228,058 qing, with official land comprising only one-seventh of private land.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年，霍韞奉命修會典，言：「自洪武迄弘治百四十年，天下額田已減強半，而湖廣、河南、廣東失額尤多。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing, Huo Yun was ordered to revise the Collected Statutes and said: "From Hongwu to Hongzhi, one hundred forty years — quota land in the empire had already diminished by more than half; Huguang, Henan, and Guangdong lost quota especially much.
translations.idiomatic: In 1529 Huo Yun, compiling the institutional code, said: "Over the 140 years from Hongwu to Hongzhi, registered quota land had shrunk by more than half, with Huguang, Henan, and Guangdong showing the steepest losses.

sentences.zh: 非撥給於王府，則欺隱於猾民。

translations.literal: If not allocated to princely establishments, then concealed by crafty commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Lost acreage had either been granted to princely estates or hidden by powerful local elites.

sentences.zh: 廣東無籓府，非欺隱即委棄於寇賊矣。

translations.literal: Guangdong had no feudatory princely residence; if not concealment, then abandonment to bandits and rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong, lacking princely estates, could only mean concealment or abandonment to bandits.

sentences.zh: 司國計者，可不究心？」

translations.literal: Those who manage the national accounts — can they fail to apply their minds?"
translations.idiomatic: Should those responsible for national finances not investigate thoroughly?"

sentences.zh: 是時，桂萼、郭弘化、唐能、簡霄先後疏請核實田畝，而顧鼎臣請履畝丈量，丈量之議由此起。

translations.literal: At this time Gui E, Guo Honghua, Tang Neng, and Jian Xiao successively memorialized requesting verification of fields and mu; Gu Dingchen requested measuring mu on the ground — the proposal for land survey thus arose.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E, Guo Honghua, Tang Neng, and Jian Xiao then petitioned for land verification; Gu Dingchen proposed on-the-ground measurement — launching the surveying movement.

sentences.zh: 江西安福、河南裕州首行之，而法未詳具，人多疑憚。

translations.literal: Anfu in Jiangxi and Yuzhou in Henan took the lead in implementing it, but the law was not fully detailed and many people doubted and feared.
translations.idiomatic: Anfu (Jiangxi) and Yuzhou (Henan) pioneered the practice, but incomplete regulations bred widespread reluctance.

sentences.zh: 其後福建諸州縣，為經、緯二冊，其法頗詳。

translations.literal: Thereafter various prefectures and counties in Fujian made warp-and-weft double registers; the method was quite detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fujian counties developed detailed dual warp-and-weft registers.

sentences.zh: 然率以地為主，田多者猶得上下其手。

translations.literal: Yet for the most part they took land as primary; those with much land could still manipulate figures up and down.
translations.idiomatic: Because registers still centered on land rather than owners, wealthy landowners could still manipulate figures.

sentences.zh: 神宗初，建昌知府許孚遠為歸戶冊，則以田從人，法簡而密矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenzong's reign, Jianchang prefect Xu Fuyuan made return-to-household registers that attached fields to persons — the law was simple yet thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli's reign, Jianchang prefect Xu Fuyuan devised household-centered registers linking fields to owners — simpler and tighter.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年，帝用大學士張居正議，天下田畝通行丈量，限三載竣事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli the emperor adopted Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng's proposal: land mu throughout the empire were universally measured on the ground, with a limit of three years for completion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1578 Wanli adopted Zhang Juzheng's plan for empire-wide land surveys, to be completed within three years.

sentences.zh: 用開方法，以徑圍乘除，畸零截補。

translations.literal: They used the opening method, multiplying and dividing diameter and circumference, trimming and supplementing irregular remainder plots.
translations.idiomatic: Surveyors applied geometric methods, calculating from diameters and perimeters and adjusting irregular plots.

sentences.zh: 於是豪猾不得欺隱，裏甲免賠累，而小民無虛糧。

translations.literal: Thereupon the powerful and crafty could not conceal; li-jia were spared compensatory burdens; and common people had no fictitious grain tax.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful evaders could no longer hide holdings, li-jia heads escaped compensatory tax shortfalls, and smallholders shed fictitious tax burdens.

sentences.zh: 總計田數七百一萬三千九百七十六頃，視弘治時贏三百萬頃。

translations.literal: The total reckoned field count was seven million one hundred three thousand nine hundred seventy-six qing — three million qing more than in the Hongzhi period.
translations.idiomatic: The survey registered 7,103,976 qing — three million more than under Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 然居正尚綜核，頗以溢額為功。

translations.literal: Yet Juzheng valued comprehensive verification and took inflated quotas somewhat as merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhang Juzheng's zeal for fiscal verification encouraged inflating reported acreage.

sentences.zh: 有司爭改小弓以求田多，或掊克見田以充虛額。

translations.literal: Local officials competed to alter to smaller measuring bows to seek more fields, or extorted existing fields to fill fictitious quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials shrank measuring rods to inflate acreage or squeezed existing fields to meet phantom quotas.

sentences.zh: 北直隸、湖廣、大同、宣府，遂先後按溢額田增賦云。

translations.literal: Zhili north of the capital, Huguang, Datong, and Xuanfu thereupon in succession levied increased tax according to inflated-quota fields.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili, Huguang, Datong, and Xuanfu subsequently raised taxes on this inflated acreage.

sentences.zh: 屯田之制：曰軍屯，曰民屯。

translations.literal: The system for colony fields had two kinds: military colonies and commoner colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Colony land fell into two types: military colonies and civilian colonies.

sentences.zh: 太祖初，立民兵萬戶府，寓兵於農，其法最善。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Taizu established the Militia Myriad-Household Office, lodging troops in farming — its law was finest.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Hongwu established militia units combining farming and military service — the ideal arrangement.

sentences.zh: 又令諸將屯兵龍江諸處，惟康茂才績最，乃下令褒之，因以申飭將士。

translations.literal: He also ordered generals to station troops in colonies at Longjiang and elsewhere; only Kang Maocai's achievements were greatest, whereupon he issued an order commending him and thereby admonished officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered generals to establish garrison farms along the Longjiang; Kang Maocai's outstanding results won imperial praise and served as a model for other commanders.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，中書省請稅太原、朔州屯卒，命勿徵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu the Secretariat requested taxing colony troops at Taiyuan and Shuozhou; he ordered that it not be levied.
translations.idiomatic: In 1370 when the central government proposed taxing Taiyuan and Shuozhou garrison farms, Hongwu refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，中書省言：「河南、山東、北平、陝西、山西及直隸淮安諸府屯田，凡官給牛種者十稅五，自備者十稅三。」

translations.literal: The next year the Secretariat said: "Colony fields in Henan, Shandong, Beiping, Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Huai'an and other prefectures of Zhili — where the state gave oxen and seed, tax five in ten; self-provided, three in ten."
translations.idiomatic: The following year officials said: "For garrison farms in Henan, Shandong, Beiping, Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Huai'an in Zhili, those with state-supplied oxen and seed pay five-tenths tax, and self-equipped ones pay three-tenths."

sentences.zh: 詔且勿徵，三年後畝收租一斗。

translations.literal: An edict said for the time being not to levy; three years later collect one dou rent per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu postponed collection, setting a rate of one dou per mu after three years.

sentences.zh: 六年，太僕丞樑埜仙帖木爾言：「寧夏境內及四川西南至船城，東北至塔灘，相去八百里，土膏沃，宜招集流亡屯田。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year Palace Stud Deputy Liang Ye Xiantiemuer said: "Within Ningxia and in Sichuan from the southwest to Chuancheng, northeast to Tatan — eight hundred li apart — the soil is rich and fertile; it is fitting to recruit and gather displaced persons for colony farming."
translations.idiomatic: In 1373 Palace Stud Deputy Liang Ye Xiantiemuer said: "Within Ningxia and in Sichuan from the southwest to Chuancheng and northeast to Tatan — eight hundred li apart — the soil is rich; displaced persons should be recruited for garrison farming."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The proposal] was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 是時，遣鄧愈、湯和諸將屯陝西、彰德、汝甯、北平、永平，徙山西真定民屯鳳陽。

translations.literal: At this time Deng Yu, Tang He, and other generals were dispatched to colonize Shaanxi, Zhangde, Runing, Beiping, and Yongping; people of Shanxi and Zhending were moved to colonize at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Generals including Deng Yu and Tang He established colonies across Shaanxi, Zhangde, Runing, Beiping, and Yongping, while people of Shanxi and Zhending were moved to colonize Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 又因海運餉遼有溺死者，遂益講屯政，天下衛所州縣軍民皆事墾闢矣。

translations.literal: Also because there were drowned men in sea transport of grain supplies to Liao, colony policy was increasingly discussed; military and civilians in guards, posts, prefectures, and counties throughout the empire all engaged in opening wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: After drownings during sea transport of grain to Liaodong, the government intensified garrison farming empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 其制，移民就寬鄉，或召募或罪徙者為民屯，皆領之有司，而軍屯則領之衛所。

translations.literal: Its regulations: migrants to spacious districts, or recruits, or those banished for crimes served as commoner colonies — all supervised by civil officials; military colonies were supervised by guards and posts.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian colonies settled migrants, recruits, or convicts under civil administration; military colonies fell under guard units.

sentences.zh: 邊地，三分守城，七分屯種。

translations.literal: In border regions, three parts garrisoning cities, seven parts colony cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier, 30% of troops garrisoned while 70% farmed.

sentences.zh: 內地，二分守城，八分屯種。

translations.literal: In interior regions, two parts garrisoning, eight parts cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: In the interior, the ratio was 20% garrison duty to 80% farming.

sentences.zh: 每軍受田五十畝為一分，給耕牛、農具，教樹植，復租賦，遣官勸輸，誅侵暴之吏。

translations.literal: Each soldier received fifty mu as one share, was given plow oxen and farm tools, taught planting, had rent and tax remitted, officials were sent to encourage delivery, and oppressive officers were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Each soldier received a fifty-mu plot with oxen and tools, tax exemptions, agricultural instruction, official encouragement to deliver harvests, and punishment for abusive local officials.

sentences.zh: 初畝稅一斗。

translations.literal: At first one dou tax per mu.
translations.idiomatic: The initial rate was one dou per mu.

sentences.zh: 三十五年定科則：軍田一分，正糧十二石，貯屯倉，聽本軍自支，餘糧為本衛所官軍俸糧。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year tax categories were fixed: one military-field share — principal grain twelve shi, stored in colony granaries, permitting the unit to draw for itself; surplus grain served as salary grain for officers and soldiers of the guard or post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1402 regulations fixed each fifty-mu share at twelve shi of principal grain stored in colony granaries for the unit's use, with surplus funding guard payrolls.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，定屯田官軍賞罰例：歲食米十二石外餘六石為率，多者賞鈔，缺者罰俸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, reward and punishment regulations for colony officers and soldiers were fixed: beyond twelve shi of rice consumed per year, a surplus of six shi was the standard; more brought paper-money reward, shortfall brought salary penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle's reign, garrison farmers who produced six shi beyond the twelve-shi subsistence quota earned bonuses; shortfalls incurred pay cuts.

sentences.zh: 又以田肥瘠不同，法宜有別，命官軍各種樣田，以其歲收之數相考較。

translations.literal: Also because fields differed in fertility and leanness, the law should differ; he ordered officers and soldiers each to plant model fields, comparing annual harvest figures thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Because soil fertility varied, Yongle ordered each unit to plant sample fields for yield comparison.

sentences.zh: 太原左衛千戶陳淮所種樣田，每軍餘糧二十三石，帝命重賞之。

translations.literal: Chen Huai, chiliarch of Taiyuan Left Guard, planted model fields; each soldier had surplus grain of twenty-three shi; the emperor ordered heavy reward.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huai of Taiyuan Left Guard achieved twenty-three shi surplus per soldier on his sample fields, earning substantial imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 寧夏總兵何福積谷尤多，賜敕褒美。

translations.literal: Ningxia regional commander He Fu accumulated grain especially much; an imperial letter of praise was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia commander He Fu's exceptional grain stores earned an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書鬱新言：「湖廣諸衛收糧不一種，請以米為準。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Yu Xin said: "Various guards in Huguang collect grain not of one type; we request taking rice as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Minister Yu Xin said: "Grain collections among Huguang garrisons vary by type; we propose standardizing on rice.

sentences.zh: 凡粟穀穈黍大麥蕎穄二石，稻穀薥秫二石五斗，穇稗三石，皆準米一石。

translations.literal: All millet, grain, broomcorn millet, barley, buckwheat two shi; husked rice, sorghum two shi five dou; coarse cereals three shi — all equaled one shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Conversion rates fixed two shi of millet, barley, or buckwheat; two and a half shi of rice or sorghum; and three shi of inferior grains as equivalent to one shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 小麥芝麻豆與米等。」

translations.literal: Wheat, sesame, and beans equaled rice."
translations.idiomatic: Wheat, sesame, and beans should count equal to rice by volume."

sentences.zh: 從之，著為令。

translations.literal: [The proposal] was approved and established as statute.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved and codified these rates.

sentences.zh: 又更定屯守之數。

translations.literal: Colony garrison numbers were also re-fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison-farm ratios were also revised.

sentences.zh: 臨邊險要，守多於屯。

translations.literal: Along dangerous border points, garrisoning exceeded colonies.
translations.idiomatic: At critical border posts, more troops garrisoned than farmed.

sentences.zh: 地僻處及輸糧艱者，屯多於守，屯兵百名委百戶，三百名委千戶，五百名以上指揮提督之。

translations.literal: In remote places and where grain transport was difficult, colonies exceeded garrisoning; one hundred colony soldiers were entrusted to a centurion, three hundred to a chiliarch, five hundred or more to a commander as supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Remote posts with difficult supply lines assigned more farmers than garrison soldiers, with centurions commanding 100 colonists, chiliarchs 300, and commanders supervising 500 or more.

sentences.zh: 屯設紅牌，列則例於上。

translations.literal: Colonies set up red placards, listing regulations and precedents upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Each colony posted red placards listing regulations.

sentences.zh: 年六十與殘疾及幼者，耕以自食，不限於例。

translations.literal: Those sixty years of age, disabled, and the young — farming to feed themselves — were not limited by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers over sixty, disabled, or too young farmed for subsistence without quota restrictions.

sentences.zh: 屯軍以公事妨農務者，免徵子粒，且禁衛所差撥。

translations.literal: Colony soldiers whose public duties obstructed farm work were exempt from grain levy, and guard-post requisitioning was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Colonists diverted from farming by official duties were exempted from grain levies, and arbitrary guard requisitions were banned.

sentences.zh: 於時，東自遼左，北抵宣、大，西至甘肅，南盡滇、蜀，極於交阯，中原則大河南北，在在興屯矣。

translations.literal: At this time, east from Liaodong left, north reaching Xuanfu and Datong, west to Gansu, south through Yunnan and Sichuan to the limit of Jiaozhi, in the central plain then north and south of the Great River — everywhere colonies flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Colonies stretched from Liaodong west to Gansu, south through Yunnan and Sichuan to Jiaozhi, and across central China — garrison farming flourished empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 宣宗之世，屢核各屯，以征戍罷耕及官豪勢要佔匿者，減餘糧之半。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign, colonies were repeatedly audited; those where campaigns halted farming and official, powerful, and influential persons concealed holdings had surplus grain reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande repeatedly audited colonies, halving surplus-grain quotas where campaigns interrupted farming or elites had seized land.

sentences.zh: 迤北來歸就屯之人，給車牛農器。

translations.literal: People coming from the far north to submit and join colonies were given carts, oxen, and farm implements.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal peoples submitting from the northern frontier received carts, cattle, and tools.

sentences.zh: 分遼東各衛屯軍為三等，丁牛兼者為上，丁牛有一為中，俱無者為下。

translations.literal: Colony soldiers of various guards in Liaodong were divided into three grades: those with both adult males and oxen were upper; with one of the two, middle; with neither, lower.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong colonies ranked soldiers by resources: top grade had both labor and oxen, middle had one, bottom had neither.

sentences.zh: 英宗免軍田正糧歸倉，止徵餘糧六石。

translations.literal: Yingzong remitted principal grain of military fields returning to granaries; only surplus grain of six shi was levied.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong waived principal-grain deposits to colony granaries, taxing only the six-shi surplus quota.

sentences.zh: 後又免沿邊開田官軍子粒，減各邊屯田子粒有差。

translations.literal: Later he also remitted grain levy on frontier opened fields for officers and soldiers, reducing colony grain levies on each frontier with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Later he exempted frontier reclaimed land from levies and reduced border colony taxes variably.

sentences.zh: 景帝時，邊方多事，令兵分為兩番，六日操守，六日耕種。

translations.literal: In Jingdi's time the frontier had many affairs; he ordered troops divided into two shifts — six days on guard, six days farming.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingtai's reign frontier turmoil required alternating six-day garrison and six-day farming shifts.

sentences.zh: 成化初，宣府巡撫葉盛買官牛千八百，並置農具，遣軍屯田，收糧易銀，以補官馬耗損，邊入稱便。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, Xuanfu grand coordinator Ye Sheng bought one thousand eight hundred official oxen and also provided farm tools, dispatched troops to colony farm, collected grain exchanged for silver to supplement official horse losses — border people called it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In 1465 Xuanfu coordinator Ye Sheng purchased 1,800 oxen and tools for garrison farming, converting grain to silver for cavalry maintenance — a welcomed frontier reform.

sentences.zh: 自正統後，屯政稍弛，而屯糧猶存三之二。

translations.literal: From after Zhengtong, colony administration gradually slackened, yet colony grain still retained two of three parts.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhengtong era colony administration slackened, though roughly two-thirds of grain levies remained.

sentences.zh: 其後屯田多為內監、軍官佔奪，法盡壞。

translations.literal: Thereafter colony fields were largely seized by inner eunuchs and military officers; the law was utterly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually eunuchs and officers seized most colony land, destroying the system.

sentences.zh: 憲宗之世頗議釐復，而視舊所入，不能什一矣。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's reign there was much discussion of rectification and restoration, but compared with old receipts it could not reach one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua saw restoration efforts, but revenues reached less than a tenth of former levels.

sentences.zh: 弘治間，屯糧愈輕，有畝止三升者。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period colony grain grew ever lighter; in places there were only three sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: By Hongzhi colony grain levies had fallen so low that some fields paid only three sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 沿及正德，遼東屯田較永樂間田贏萬八千餘頃，而糧乃縮四萬六千餘石。

translations.literal: Extending to Zhengde, Liaodong colony fields compared with Yongle-era fields gained more than eighteen thousand surplus qing, yet grain shrank by more than forty-six thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhengde Liaodong registered 18,000 more qing than under Yongle yet collected 46,000 fewer shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 初，永樂時，屯田米常溢三之一，常操軍十九萬，以屯軍四萬供之。

translations.literal: At first, in Yongle times, colony rice often exceeded by one-third; regularly stationed troops were one hundred ninety thousand, supplied by forty thousand colony troops.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle colony grain usually exceeded quotas by a third; 190,000 regular troops were fed by 40,000 colonists.

sentences.zh: 而受供者又得自耕。

translations.literal: Those who received supplies could also farm for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Recipients of colony grain could still farm additional land for themselves.

sentences.zh: 邊外軍無月糧，以是邊餉恆足。

translations.literal: Troops outside the border had no monthly grain ration; thereby border supplies were constantly sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops beyond the wall lacked monthly rations, yet border supplies remained adequate.

sentences.zh: 及是，屯軍多逃死，常操軍止八萬，皆仰給於倉。

translations.literal: By this time many colony soldiers had fled or died; regularly stationed troops were only eighty thousand, all relying on granary supply.
translations.idiomatic: By then colonists had fled or died in large numbers; only 80,000 regular troops remained, all dependent on state granaries.

sentences.zh: 而邊外數擾，棄不耕。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the outer border was repeatedly disturbed and abandoned, left uncultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier disturbances left outer-border land fallow.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾擅政，遣官分出丈田責逋。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin monopolized power, he sent out officials to measure fields separately and demand arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Jin's dictatorship, officials were dispatched to survey land and collect back taxes.

sentences.zh: 希瑾意者，偽增田數，蒐括慘毒，戶部侍郎韓福尤急刻。

translations.literal: Those who hoped to please Jin falsely inflated field counts, searched and squeezed cruelly; Vice Minister of Revenue Han Fu was especially harsh and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Officials currying favor fabricated acreage and extorted brutally — Vice Minister Han Fu among the worst.

sentences.zh: 遼卒不堪，脅眾為亂，撫之乃定。

translations.literal: Liaodong soldiers could not bear it; they coerced the masses into rebellion — only after pacification was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: Unbearable oppression drove Liaodong troops to mutiny, quelled only after pacification.

sentences.zh: 明初，募鹽商於各邊開中，謂之商屯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming, salt merchants were recruited at each border for kaizhong (frontier grain-salt exchange); this was called merchant colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, salt merchants were recruited to the frontiers for the kaizhong grain-salt exchange system — estates known as merchant colonies.

sentences.zh: 迨弘治中，葉淇變法，而開中始壞。

translations.literal: By the Hongzhi reign, Ye Qi changed the law, and kaizhong began to break down.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, Ye Qi's reforms broke the kaizhong system for the first time.

sentences.zh: 諸淮商悉撤業歸，西北商亦多徙家於淮，邊地為墟，米石直銀五兩，而邊儲枵然矣。

translations.literal: All Huai merchants completely withdrew from their trade and returned home; northwestern merchants also mostly moved their households to the Huai region — border areas became wasteland, rice reached five taels of silver per shi, and border storage was utterly depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Huai salt merchants abandoned their businesses entirely; northwestern merchants too moved families to the Huai region. Borderlands turned to wasteland, grain hit five taels of silver per shi, and frontier granaries stood empty.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，楊一清復請召商開中，又請仿古募民實塞下之意，招徠隴右、關西民以屯邊。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign, Yang Yiqing again petitioned to summon merchants for kaizhong; he also petitioned to follow the ancient meaning of recruiting commoners to settle and fill the frontier passes, soliciting people from Longyou and Guanxi to colonize the border.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing, Yang Yiqing again urged restoring merchant kaizhong and, following ancient precedent, recruiting Longyou and Guanxi settlers to farm the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其後周澤、王崇古、林富、陳世輔、王畿、王朝用、唐順之、吳桂芳等爭言屯政。

translations.literal: Thereafter Zhou Ze, Wang Chonggu, Lin Fu, Chen Shifu, Wang Ji, Wang Chaoyong, Tang Shunzhi, Wu Guifang, and others vied to speak on colony policy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Zhou Ze, Wang Chonggu, Lin Fu, Chen Shifu, Wang Ji, Wang Chaoyong, Tang Shunzhi, Wu Guifang, and others all pressed proposals on garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 而龐尚鵬總理江北鹽屯，尋移九邊，與總督王崇古，先後區畫屯政甚詳。

translations.literal: Pang Shangpeng oversaw salt colonies on the north bank of the Yangzi, soon transferred to the nine border zones; with governor-general Wang Chonggu he successively laid out colony policy in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shangpeng directed salt colonies along the north Yangzi, then moved to the nine frontier commands, working with Governor-General Wang Chonggu to draft detailed colony plans.

sentences.zh: 然是時因循日久，卒鮮實效。

translations.literal: Yet by this time delay through routine had lasted long; in the end there was little real effect.
translations.idiomatic: But years of bureaucratic inertia left little lasting result.

sentences.zh: 給事中管懷理言：「屯田不興，其弊有四：疆埸戒嚴，一也；

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Guan Huaili said: "Colony fields do not flourish; their abuses are fourfold: the frontier is on strict alert — the first;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Guan Huaili said: "Garrison farms fail to thrive. There are four abuses: strict frontier alerts — first;

sentences.zh: 牛種不給，二也；

translations.literal: oxen and seed are not supplied — the second;
translations.idiomatic: no oxen or seed provided — second;

sentences.zh: 丁壯亡徙，三也；

translations.literal: able-bodied men have fled and migrated — the third;
translations.idiomatic: able-bodied men have fled — third;

sentences.zh: 田在敵外，四也。

translations.literal: fields lie beyond the enemy — the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: fields lie beyond enemy lines — fourth.

sentences.zh: 如是而管屯者猶欲按籍增賦，非扣月糧，即按丁賠補耳。」

translations.literal: Yet under these conditions those who administer colonies still wish to increase levies according to the register — if not deducting monthly grain rations, then assessing per-capita compensation."
translations.idiomatic: Yet colony administrators still seek higher levies from the registers — deducting monthly rations or exacting per-capita payments."

sentences.zh: 屯糧之輕，至弘、正而極，嘉靖中漸增，隆慶間復畝收一斗。

translations.literal: Lightness of colony grain [burden] reached its extreme in the Hongzhi and Zhengde reigns; in Jiajing it gradually increased; in Longqing per-mu collection of one dou was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Colony grain levies were lightest under Hongzhi and Zhengde, rose through Jiajing, and in Longqing the one-dou-per-mu rate returned.

sentences.zh: 然屯丁逃亡者益多。

translations.literal: Yet colony laborers who fled grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Colony laborers deserted in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 管糧郎中不問屯田有無，月糧止半給。

translations.literal: The director in charge of grain did not inquire whether colony fields existed; monthly grain was only half issued.
translations.idiomatic: Grain administrators ignored whether fields were actually farmed and paid only half the monthly ration.

sentences.zh: 沿邊屯地，或變為斥鹵、沙磧，糧額不得減。

translations.literal: Along the border, colony land sometimes turned to salt marsh and sandy waste, yet grain quotas could not be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Border colony land often turned saline or sandy, yet tax quotas could not be lowered.

sentences.zh: 屯田御史又於額外增本折，屯軍益不堪命。

translations.literal: The colony-field censor again added principal conversion on top of quotas; colony soldiers could bear the command even less.
translations.idiomatic: Colony censors piled extra principal conversions on quotas, crushing garrison farmers further.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，計屯田之數六十四萬四千餘頃，視洪武時虧二十四萬九千餘頃，田日減而糧日增，其弊如此。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, colony fields were reckoned at 644,000-odd qing; compared with Hongwu times there was a shortfall of 249,000-odd qing — fields daily diminished while grain daily increased; such were the abuses.
translations.idiomatic: By Wanli, registered colony land totaled 644,000-odd qing — 249,000 qing less than under Hongwu — while levies rose as acreage shrank.

sentences.zh: 時則山東巡撫鄭汝璧請開登州海北長山諸島田。

translations.literal: At the time Shandong provincial grand coordinator Zheng Rubi petitioned to open fields on the islands of Changshan and others north of the sea at Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Grand Coordinator Zheng Rubi proposed opening farmland on the Changshan islands off northern Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 福建巡撫許孚遠墾閩海壇山田成，復請開南日山、澎湖；

translations.literal: Fujian grand coordinator Xu Fuyuan successfully reclaimed fields on Tan Mountain in the Fujian sea, and again petitioned to open Niri Mountain and Penghu;
translations.idiomatic: Fujian Grand Coordinator Xu Fuyuan reclaimed Tan Mountain in the Fujian straits and petitioned to open Niri Mountain and Penghu;

sentences.zh: 又言浙江濱海諸山，若陳錢、金塘、補陀、玉環、南麂，皆可經理。

translations.literal: he also said that coastal mountains of Zhejiang — such as Chenqian, Jintang, Putuo, Yuhuan, and Nanji — could all be managed.
translations.idiomatic: he also urged developing Zhejiang's coastal islands — Chenqian, Jintang, Putuo, Yuhuan, Nanji, and others.

sentences.zh: 天津巡撫汪應蛟則請於天津興屯。

translations.literal: Tianjin grand coordinator Wang Yingjiao petitioned to promote colonies at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin Grand Coordinator Wang Yingjiao urged expanding garrison farms around Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 或留中不下，或不久輒廢。

translations.literal: Some memorials were retained at court and not issued; others were soon abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposals languished at court; others were tried briefly then dropped.

sentences.zh: 熹宗之世，巡按張慎言復議天津屯田。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign, touring censor Zhang Shenyan again discussed Tianjin colony fields.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi, Touring Censor Zhang Shenyan revived the Tianjin colony proposal.

sentences.zh: 而御史左光鬥命管河通判盧觀象大興水田之利，太常少卿董應舉踵而行之。

translations.literal: Censor Zuo Guangdou ordered river intendant Lu Guanxiang greatly to expand the benefits of paddy fields; Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dong Yingju followed in carrying this out.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zuo Guangdou ordered River Intendant Lu Guanxiang to expand paddy cultivation; Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dong Yingju continued the effort.

sentences.zh: 光鬥更於河間、天津設屯學，試騎射，為武生給田百畝。

translations.literal: Guangdou further established colony schools at Hejian and Tianjin, tested horsemanship and archery, and granted military students one hundred mu of fields each.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Guangdou founded colony schools at Hejian and Tianjin, tested horsemanship and archery, and granted each military student one hundred mu.

sentences.zh: 李繼貞巡撫天津，亦力於屯務，然仍歲旱蝗，弗克底成效也。

translations.literal: Li Jizhen as Tianjin grand coordinator also exerted himself in colony affairs, yet year after year there were drought and locusts; he could not bring matters to final effect.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Li Jizhen pressed colony work equally hard, but drought and locusts year after year prevented lasting success.

sentences.zh: 明時，草場頗多，佔奪民業。

translations.literal: In the Ming period, pasture grounds were rather numerous and seized commoners' livelihoods.
