translations.idiomatic: Ming pasture reserves were extensive and often seized from commoners.

sentences.zh: 而為民厲者，莫如皇莊及諸王、勳戚、中官莊田為甚。

translations.literal: Yet what harmed the people most severely were imperial estates and the estate fields of princes, meritorious kinsmen, and eunuch officials.
translations.idiomatic: The worst scourges were imperial estates and manor lands held by princes, noble kinsmen, and eunuch officials.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜勳臣公侯丞相以下莊田，多者百頃，親王莊田千頃。

translations.literal: Taizu granted estate fields to meritorious officials from dukes and marquises and chancellors downward — at most one hundred qing; princely estate fields one thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu granted manor estates to meritorious officials from dukes and marquises down — up to one hundred qing; princes received up to one thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 又賜公侯暨武臣公田，又賜百官公田，以其租入充祿。

translations.literal: He also granted public fields to dukes and marquises and military officials, and also granted public fields to officials of all ranks, using their rents to supply salaries.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted public salary fields to nobles, military officers, and civil officials, whose rents funded their stipends.

sentences.zh: 指揮沒於陣者皆賜公田。

translations.literal: Commanders who died in battle were all granted public fields.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders killed in battle received public fields as well.

sentences.zh: 勳臣莊佃，多倚威捍禁，帝召諸臣戒諭之。

translations.literal: Meritorious officials' estate tenants mostly relied on power to defy prohibition; the emperor summoned the various ministers and admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: Noble estate tenants often bullied neighbors with impunity until the emperor summoned ministers to warn them.

sentences.zh: 其後公侯復歲祿，歸賜田於官。

translations.literal: Thereafter dukes and marquises again received annual salaries and returned granted fields to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Later nobles resumed annual stipends and returned granted fields to the state.

sentences.zh: 仁、宣之世，乞請漸廣，大臣亦得請沒官莊舍。

translations.literal: In the Hongxi and Xuande reigns, petitions and requests gradually widened; great ministers also could request confiscated manor estates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongxi and Xuande, land petitions multiplied, and even senior ministers could request confiscated manors.

sentences.zh: 然甯王權請灌城為庶子耕牧地，帝賜書，援祖制拒之。

translations.literal: Yet the Prince of Ning, Quan, petitioned for Guancheng as land for his sons to farm and herd; the emperor bestowed a written reply citing ancestral regulation to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Ning Zhu Quan sought Guancheng for his sons to farm, the emperor refused by citing ancestral precedent.

sentences.zh: 至英宗時，諸王、外戚、中官所在佔官私田，或反誣民佔，請案治。

translations.literal: By the Yingzong reign, princes, maternal kindred, and eunuch officials everywhere occupied official and private fields — or inversely accused commoners of occupation and petitioned for investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yingzong, princes, consort kin, and eunuch officials seized public and private land everywhere — sometimes accusing peasants of trespass to have them prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 比案問得實，帝命還之民者非一。

translations.literal: When investigations found the facts, the emperor ordered return to the commoners — not once only.
translations.idiomatic: When investigations proved the facts, the emperor repeatedly ordered land returned to peasants.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔禁奪民田及奏請畿內地。

translations.literal: Then an edict was issued forbidding seizure of commoners' fields and memorial petitions for land within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then forbade seizing peasant land and petitioning for plots in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 然權貴宗室莊田墳塋，或賜或請，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Yet estate fields and tombs of powerful and noble clans were granted or petitioned for beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet powerful clans still received countless grants of manor land and tomb estates.

sentences.zh: 御馬太監劉順家人進薊州草場，進獻由此始。

translations.literal: The household of Imperial Horse Supervisor Liu Shun presented Jizhou pasture grounds — thus presentation of land began.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Horse Supervisor Liu Shun's household presented Jizhou pastureland — beginning the practice of land presentation.

sentences.zh: 宦官之田，則自尹奉、喜寧始。

translations.literal: Estate fields of eunuchs began with Yin Feng and Xi Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch manor estates began with Yin Feng and Xi Ning.

sentences.zh: 初，洪熙時，有仁壽宮莊，其後又有清寧、未央宮莊。

translations.literal: At first, in the Hongxi reign, there was the Renshou Palace estate; afterward there were also the Qingning and Weiyang palace estates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongxi came the Renshou Palace estate, followed by Qingning and Weiyang palace estates.

sentences.zh: 天順三年，以諸王未出閣，供用浩繁，立東宮、德王、秀王莊田。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshun, because princes had not yet left the palace to take up fiefs and expenses were vast, estate fields were established for the Heir Apparent, Prince of De, and Prince of Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 3, with princes still in the capital and expenses heavy, estates were set up for the heir apparent and the Princes of De and Xiu.

sentences.zh: 二王之籓，地仍歸官。

translations.literal: When the two princes went to their fiefs, the land again reverted to the government.
translations.idiomatic: When those two princes departed for their fiefs, the land reverted to the state.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，以沒入曹吉祥地為宮中莊田，皇莊之名由此始。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, confiscated lands of Cao Jixiang became palace estate fields — the name imperial estates began here.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenghua took the throne, Cao Jixiang's confiscated property became palace estates — the term imperial estates dates from this.

sentences.zh: 其後莊田遍郡縣。

translations.literal: Thereafter estate fields spread through prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Manor estates soon spread through every prefecture and county.

sentences.zh: 給事中齊莊言：「天子以四海為家，何必置立莊田，與貧民較利。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Qi Zhuang said: "The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his house — why must estate fields be set up to contend for profit with poor commoners?"
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Qi Zhuang said: "The Son of Heaven owns the four seas — why establish manor estates to squeeze profit from the poor?"

sentences.zh: 弗聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，戶部尚書李敏等以災異上言：「畿內皇莊有五，共地萬二千八百餘頃；

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi, Minister of Revenue Li Min and others, citing calamities and anomalies, memorialized: "Within the capital region there are five imperial estates, together 12,800-odd qing of land;
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 2, Revenue Minister Li Min and others, citing omens and disasters, reported: "In the capital region there are five imperial estates totaling 12,800-odd qing;

sentences.zh: 勳戚、中官莊田三百三十有二，共地三萬三千餘頃。

translations.literal: meritorious kinsmen and eunuch officials' estate fields number three hundred thirty-two, together 33,000-odd qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: noble and eunuch estates number 332, totaling 33,000-odd qing.

sentences.zh: 管莊官校招集羣小，稱莊頭、伴當，佔地土，斂財物，汙婦女。

translations.literal: Managing officials and military retainers recruit riffraff called estate heads and attendants; they seize land, extort goods, and violate women.
translations.idiomatic: Estate managers and retainers recruit thugs as estate heads and attendants, seize land, extort goods, and assault women.

sentences.zh: 稍與分辯，輒被誣奏。

translations.literal: If one slightly argues with them, one is immediately falsely memorialized against.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who disputes them faces false accusations.

sentences.zh: 官校執縛，舉家驚惶。

translations.literal: Official retainers bind and arrest; whole families are panic-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: Official retainers bind and arrest them; whole families live in terror.

sentences.zh: 民心傷痛入骨，災異所由生。

translations.literal: Popular hearts are wounded to the marrow — whence calamities and anomalies arise.
translations.idiomatic: Popular resentment runs bone-deep — the source of heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 乞革去管莊之人，付小民耕種，畝徵銀三分，充各宮用度。」

translations.literal: We beg to abolish those who manage estates, hand [land] to commoners to farm, and levy three fen of silver per mu to supply each palace's expenses."
translations.idiomatic: We beg to remove estate managers, let peasants farm the land, and levy three fen of silver per mu for palace expenses."

sentences.zh: 帝命戒飭莊戶。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered admonition of estate tenants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor merely ordered estate tenants admonished.

sentences.zh: 又因御史言，罷仁壽宮莊，還之草場，且命凡侵牧地者，悉還其舊。

translations.literal: Again following a censor's memorial, the Renshou Palace estate was abolished and returned to pasture; moreover it was ordered that all who encroached on pasture land should restore it to the former state.
translations.idiomatic: Following a censor's memorial, the Renshou Palace estate was abolished and restored to pasture; encroachers on pastureland were ordered to return it.

sentences.zh: 又定制，獻地王府者戍邊。

translations.literal: Regulations were also fixed: those presenting land to princely mansions were punished with frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: A rule was set: presenting land to princely mansions earned frontier-service punishment.

sentences.zh: 奉禦趙瑄獻雄縣地為皇莊，戶部尚書周經劾其違制，下瑄詔獄。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhao Xuan presented Xiong County land as an imperial estate; Minister of Revenue Zhou Jing impeached him for violating regulations and Zhao Xuan was imprisoned by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhao Xuan offered Xiong County as an imperial estate; Revenue Minister Zhou Jing impeached him for violating regulations and Zhao was jailed by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 敕諸王輔導官，導王奏請者罪之。

translations.literal: An edict commanded princes' tutoring officials: those who guided princes to memorial and request would be punished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict warned princes' tutors: any who coached memorial petitions would be punished.

sentences.zh: 然當日奏獻不絕，氣請亦愈繁。

translations.literal: Yet at that time presentations did not cease; memorial petitions also grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet land presentations never stopped and petitions grew ever more frequent.

sentences.zh: 徽、興、岐、衡四王，田多至七千餘頃。

translations.literal: The four princes of Hui, Xing, Qi, and Heng each had fields reaching as many as seven thousand-odd qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Hui, Xing, Qi, and Heng each held up to 7,000-odd qing.

sentences.zh: 會昌、建昌、慶雲三侯爭田，帝輒賜之。

translations.literal: The three marquises of Huichang, Jianchang, and Qingyun disputed fields; the emperor immediately granted them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquises of Huichang, Jianchang, and Qingyun disputed fields, the emperor granted them at once.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，逾月即建皇莊七，其後增至三百餘處。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, within a month he established seven imperial estates; thereafter they increased to more than three hundred locations.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month of Zhengde's accession, seven imperial estates were created; they eventually exceeded three hundred.

sentences.zh: 諸王、外戚求請及奪民田者無算。

translations.literal: Princes, maternal kindred, petitions and requests, and seizure of commoners' fields were beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, consort kin, petitions, and peasant land seizures became innumerable.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，命給事中夏言等清核皇莊田。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign, supervising secretaries Xia Yan and others were ordered to clear and verify imperial estate fields.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing, supervising secretaries Xia Yan and others were ordered to audit imperial estates.

sentences.zh: 言極言皇莊為厲於民。

translations.literal: Yan spoke vehemently that imperial estates were a scourge upon the people.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yan argued forcefully that imperial estates scourged the people.

sentences.zh: 自是正德以來投獻侵牟之地，頗有給還民者，而宦戚輩復中撓之。

translations.literal: From then on, lands presented and encroached upon since Zhengde were in considerable part returned to commoners, yet eunuchs and maternal kin again obstructed in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Much land seized since Zhengde was returned to peasants, but eunuchs and consort kin repeatedly blocked enforcement.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書孫交造皇莊新冊，額減於舊。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Sun Jiao compiled a new register of imperial estates; the quota was reduced from the old.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Minister Sun Jiao compiled a new imperial-estate register with lower totals than before.

sentences.zh: 帝命核先年頃畝數以聞，改稱官地，不復名皇莊，詔所司徵銀解部。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered verification of earlier years' qing and mu to be reported; [estates] were renamed official land, no longer called imperial estates; an edict ordered responsible offices to levy silver and remit to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered acreage verified, estates renamed official land rather than imperial estates, and silver levies remitted to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 然多為宦寺中飽，積逋至數十萬以為常。

translations.literal: Yet much was pocketed by eunuchs; accumulated arrears reaching hundreds of thousands became the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs pocketed much of the revenue; arrears in the hundreds of thousands became routine.

sentences.zh: 是時，禁勳戚奏討、奸民投獻者，又革王府所請山場湖陂。

translations.literal: At this time presentation by meritorious kinsmen was forbidden and scheming commoners who presented land were [restricted]; manor hills, lakes, and marshes requested by princely mansions were also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions from noble kin were banned, fraudulent land presentations curbed, and princely requests for hills, lakes, and marshes abolished.

sentences.zh: 德王請齊、漢二庶人所遺東昌、兗州閒田，又請白雲等湖，山東巡撫邵錫按新令卻之，語甚切。

translations.literal: The Prince of De requested the idle fields of Dongchang and Yanzhou left by the two lesser members of the Qi and Han lines, and also requested lakes such as Baiyun; Shandong grand coordinator Shao Xi refused according to the new order, his language very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of De sought idle Dongchang and Yanzhou fields left by Qi and Han cadet lines plus lakes such as Baiyun; Shandong Grand Coordinator Shao Xi bluntly refused under the new rules.

sentences.zh: 德王爭之數四，帝仍從部議，但存籓封初請莊田。

translations.literal: The Prince of De disputed this four times; the emperor still followed the ministry's plan, retaining only the estate fields of the initial fief petition.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of De appealed four times; the emperor upheld the ministry, keeping only his original fief allotment.

sentences.zh: 其後有奏請者不聽。

translations.literal: Thereafter memorial petitions were not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Further petitions were rejected.

sentences.zh: 又定，凡公主、國公莊田，世遠者存什三。

translations.literal: It was further fixed: for estate fields of princesses and state dukes, when generations were distant only three-tenths were retained.
translations.idiomatic: A rule fixed that distant generations of princesses and state dukes retained only three-tenths of manor estates.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十九年遣御史瀋陽清奪隱冒莊田萬六千餘頃。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Jiajing, Censor Shen Yang was dispatched to clear concealed and falsely registered estate fields of more than sixteen thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 39, Censor Shen Yang recovered more than 16,000 qing of concealed manor land.

sentences.zh: 穆宗從御史王廷瞻言，復定世次遞減之限：勳臣五世限田二百頃，戚畹七百頃至七十頃有差。

translations.literal: Muzong, following Censor Wang Tingzhan's memorial, again fixed limits for generation-by-generation reduction: meritorious officials at the fifth generation were limited to two hundred qing; maternal kin from seven hundred qing down to seventy qing in varying grades.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longqing, following Censor Wang Tingzhan, generation limits were set: meritorious families at the fifth generation capped at 200 qing; consort kin from 700 down to 70 qing by rank.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗時，承天六莊二湖地八千三百餘頃，領以中官，又聽校舍兼併，增八百八十頃，分為十二莊。

translations.literal: At first, during Shizong's reign, the six estates and two lakes of Chengtian totaled more than 8,300 qing and were administered by eunuchs; imperial guards and hereditary military retainers were also allowed to annex land, adding 880 qing, and the holdings were divided into twelve estates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing, Chengtian's six estates and two lakes totaled 8,300-odd qing under eunuch control; imperial guards and hereditary military retainers were also permitted to annex land, adding another 880 qing and creating twelve manors.

sentences.zh: 至是始領之有司，兼併者還民。

translations.literal: At this time they were first placed under civil officials; those who had merged and annexed returned [land] to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Now they passed to civil officials, and annexed land was returned to peasants.

sentences.zh: 又著令宗室買田不輸役者沒官，皇親田俱令有司徵之，如勳臣例。

translations.literal: It was also decreed that when imperial clansmen bought fields without paying corvée labor, [the land] was confiscated; all maternal-relatives' fields were ordered levied by civil officials according to the precedent of meritorious officials.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen who bought land without paying corvée forfeited it; consort-kin estates were taxed by civil officials like noble manors.

sentences.zh: 雖請乞不乏，而賜額有定，徵收有制，民害少衰止。

translations.literal: Although petitions and requests did not cease, granted quotas were fixed and collection had regulation — popular harm somewhat declined and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions continued, but fixed quotas and regulated collection eased the burden somewhat.

sentences.zh: 神宗賚予過侈，求無不獲。

translations.literal: Shenzong's largesse was excessively extravagant; requests were never denied.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli's grants were extravagantly generous — no request refused.

sentences.zh: 潞王、壽陽公主恩最渥。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu and Princess Shouyang received the deepest favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu and Princess Shouyang received the greatest favor.

sentences.zh: 而福王分封，括河南、山東、湖廣田為王莊，至四萬頃。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enfeoffed, fields of Henan, Shandong, and Huguang were swept up as princely estates — reaching forty thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enfeoffed, Henan, Shandong, and Huguang land was swept into his estate — 40,000 qing.

sentences.zh: 羣臣力爭，乃減其半。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers strove in contention; only then was it reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers protested fiercely until the grant was halved.

sentences.zh: 王府官及諸閹丈地徵稅，旁午於道，扈養廝役廩食以萬計，漁斂慘毒不忍聞。

translations.literal: Princely mansion officials and various eunuchs measured land and levied taxes crowding the roads; retinue, retainers, and lackeys' granary provisions numbered in the tens of thousands — exactions cruel and poisonous beyond bearing to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Princely staff and eunuchs measured land and levied taxes along every road; retinues and lackeys numbered in the tens of thousands — exactions too brutal to recount.

sentences.zh: 駕帖捕民，格殺莊佃，所在騷然。

translations.literal: Imperial warrants arrested commoners; they slew resisting estate tenants; everywhere was uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial warrants seized peasants; resisting tenants were killed; the realm erupted in disorder.

sentences.zh: 給事中官應震、姚宗文等屢疏諫，皆不報。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Guan Yingzhen, Yao Zongwen, and others repeatedly remonstrated by memorial — all without response.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Guan Yingzhen, Yao Zongwen, and others remonstrated repeatedly — all ignored.

sentences.zh: 時復更定勳戚莊田世次遞減法，視舊制稍寬。

translations.literal: At the time the generation-by-generation reduction law for meritorious kinsmen's estate fields was again revised, somewhat more lenient than the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Generation-reduction rules for noble estates were revised, slightly more lenient than before.

sentences.zh: 其後應議減者，輒奉詔姑留，不能革也。

translations.literal: Thereafter when reduction was discussed, they were invariably granted edicts to provisionally retain — it could not be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When reductions were proposed, edicts invariably allowed temporary retention — reform failed.

sentences.zh: 熹宗時，桂、惠、瑞三王及遂平、甯德二公主莊田，動以萬計，而魏忠賢一門，橫賜尤甚。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign, the three princes of Gui, Hui, and Rui and the two princesses of Suiping and Ningde had estate fields reckoned by the tens of thousands; and Wei Zhongxian's whole clan received especially wanton grants.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi, the Princes of Gui, Hui, and Rui and Princesses Suiping and Ningde held estates reckoned in the tens of thousands of qing; Wei Zhongxian's clan received especially lavish grants.

sentences.zh: 蓋中葉以後，莊田侵奪民業，與國相終云。

translations.literal: Thus from the mid-dynasty onward, estate fields encroached upon and seized commoners' livelihoods, enduring with the state to its end.
translations.idiomatic: From the mid-Ming onward, manor estates seized peasant livelihoods until the dynasty's fall.
